newsitem.title: FRANCE: French planters raise 96/97 sugar output estimate.
newsitem.headline: French planters raise 96/97 sugar output estimate.

text.p: French sugar beet planters said on Thursday they now expected the 1996/97 sugar crop to reach the 4.2 million tonnes produced in 1995/96.
Planters last month predicted a crop of 4.01 million tonnes.
An analyst for the CGB beet planters' federation linked the upward revision to better than expected yields.
He said higher sugar content might boost final yields to around last year's level of 9.8 tonnes per hectare.
Last week the French sugar intervention board FIRS put the 1996/97 sugar crop at 4.1 million tonnes.
FIRS also said that if harvest conditions remained favourable final output might be near the 4.199 million tonnes reached in 1995/96.
The harvest is now over in France with 85 percent of beets delivered to refineries, planters said.
Data collected by the CGB up to this week suggested a final beet yield of 55 tonnes per hectare, down from 59 tonnes last year.
But final sugar content might jump to 18.9 percent from 17.5 percent last year.
